summary: This manuscript establishes the exact gauge-invariant dressed quantum thermodynamics of ultrastrong-coupling (USC) mitochondrial crista polaritons, resolving the unphysical vacuum heating and perpetual work extraction predicted by naive bare-basis master equations. Backed by a zero-floating-point verification suite (MITO-USC-DRESSED-THERMO-CERT-1.0) featuring 18 constructive Lean 4.36.0 integer/rational theorems (0 sorry, 0 custom axioms) and 16 canonical exact-Q certificates, the author proves: (i) a universal positive zero-point energy (ZPE) shift yielding 7.456 meV at 71/87 THz resonance, crossing the 15 kBT Helfrich bending benchmark at M >= 54 modes; (ii) identical ground-state bare occupations n_virt = 64/6177 (~0.01036, exceeding bare thermal quanta by >5180x) in both Coulomb and PZW gauges, alongside exact vacuum entanglement and diamagnetic cancellation; (iii) thermodynamic passivity (W_erg = 0), proving virtual photons cannot drive ATP work, and exposing >610x spurious bare-basis heating violations of the Second Law; (iv) exact PZW canonical matter weight swaps and gauge-invariant single-branch transition matrix elements; and (v) a collective single-mode ZPE ceiling of 7.456 meV (>2.9x the +10% catalytic barrier shift), dictating 1/N dilution limits for uncoupled lipid dipoles.
strengths: Impeccable formal verification rigor with 18 constructive Lean 4 theorems and 16 exact-Q certificates with zero axioms and zero sorries.
Rigorous resolution of gauge-ambiguity paradoxes in ultrastrong-coupling cavity QED using exact Coulomb-to-PZW unitary transformations.

Comprehensive benchmarking against biological membranes, establishing precise mode-count horizons against Helfrich bending rigidities and 1/N dilution limits.
weaknesses: Heavy reliance on idealized single-mode and bilinear Hopfield models without full spatial inhomogeneities of mitochondrial cristae membranes.
